title: Subnet-aware GPU nodegroup Terraform module with composite health checks and safe rolling upgrades for Private VPC
creator: Evelyn Park
description:
Goal: build a reusable Terraform module for Private VPC deployments that provisions GPU nodegroups compatible with both ASG-style autoscaling and Karpenter, is subnet-aware, and supports safe, observable rolling upgrades. The module will encapsulate network placement (private subnets), AMI / image pinning, GPU driver handling (prebaked AMI or bootstrap DaemonSet), mixed instance type pools, node labels/taints for Redwood workloads, and composite health probes (kubelet readiness, NVIDIA driver/daemonset health, DCGM exporter metrics, and custom cluster-level GPU pressure signals).

Scope: module, integration tests (terragrunt/mini staging), upgrade/rollback procedures, Terraform docs, example overlays for both ASG-managed nodegroups and Karpenter provisioner-backed node pools. Must include observability hooks: CloudWatch/Prometheus alarms, node draining hooks, and Prometheus alerting rules for GPU health regressions.

Design notes and constraints:
- Support AWS private VPC only for initial rollout (abstraction layer for other clouds later).
- Two operation modes: managed_autoscaling (ASG + Launch Template) and provisioner_mode (Karpenter). Mode selected by boolean var; module outputs are compatible with both.
- Subnet awareness: accept list of private subnet IDs and map per-az capacity targets. Enforce AZ distribution for heterogeneous instance types.
- GPU driver strategy: allow two mutually exclusive approaches via variable: prebaked_ami (recommended for predictable driver/kernel combos) OR driver_daemonset (for faster image churn). Document trade-offs clearly.
- Upgrades: support a staged/controlled rollout using instance refresh + lifecycle hooks for ASG and API-compatible cordon/drain + node replacement policy for Karpenter. Provide a canary toggle for small percentage rollout and automatic rollback on defined health failure windows.
- Composite health checks: combine node-level kubelet readiness, NVIDIA device plugin/driver status, and DCGM exporter success rate. Implement a short-lived probe daemon on each node reporting aggregated health to a cluster-level Prometheus metric used by automated rollout guard.
- Mixed instance types & fallback: allow prioritized instance_type lists and node selectors so runtime routing can prefer smaller RTX-GPUs when available and fall back to larger types when needed. Provide capacity-fallback policy outputs consumed by Redwood's smart routing layer.
- Security: ensure IAM instance profile scoping, KMS key references for launch_template userdata secrets, and S3/GitHub artifact download restricted to VPC endpoints when using bootstrap DaemonSet.

Parameters (high level): var.vpc_id, var.private_subnet_ids, var.mode ("asg"|"karpenter"), var.instance_types (list, ordered), var.prebaked_ami_id, var.driver_daemonset_enabled (bool), var.node_labels (map), var.node_taints (list), var.min_size, var.max_size, var.desired_capacity, var.canary_percentage, var_health_window_seconds, var_enable_prometheus_metrics, var_enable_cloudwatch_alarms.

Outputs (high level): node_group_name, launch_template_id, autoscaling_group_id (if ASG), karpenter_provisioner_name (if Karpenter), subnet_affinity_map, health_metric_namespace, upgrade_plan_url (link to generated plan in S3).
acceptance_criteria: Module provisions GPU nodegroups in a test Private VPC using both ASG and Karpenter modes without manual infra edits.
Rolling upgrade workflow can execute a canary at 5% and either continue or automatically rollback based on composite health metrics within the configured window.
Composite health probe metric is emitted to Prometheus and can be used to gate an automated instance refresh; alerts trigger when GPU driver or DCGM metrics drop below threshold.
Module exposes variables for prebaked_ami vs driver_daemonset strategies and documents ordinal trade-offs in README.
Mixed instance types behave according to priority list and fallback triggers produce an annotated output consumed by routing policies.
Security review checklist completed: least privilege IAM, KMS usage documented, and artifact fetches restricted to VPC where applicable.
tasks: Write Terraform module skeleton with inputs/outputs and separate ASG/Karpenter submodules.
Implement subnet affinity mapping and per-AZ instance distribution logic.
Add Launch Template creation with AMI pinning, user-data templating, and instance profile attachment.
Implement canary rollout helpers: S3 plan writer, CloudWatch/Prometheus alarm wiring, and lifecycle hooks for graceful drain.
Create a small probe DaemonSet that aggregates kubelet + driver + DCGM status and exposes a Prometheus metric.
Document driver strategies and produce example overlay manifests for prebaked AMI and driver DaemonSet approaches.
Integration test: progressive rollout in staging cluster, force a failing DCGM exporter on canary nodes to verify rollback logic.
Add TF examples folder: asg-example.tf, karpenter-example.tf, and a terragrunt overlay for private staging.
Security review and IAM policy generation using least privilege templates; run internal security checklist.
Create CI pipeline step to run 'terraform plan' and plan validation hooks for upgrade drift detection.
